verdict: M258's core frozen-population and ready-sensitivity arithmetic is exact for its declared abstract schedule. Independent raw-CSV parsing finds 1,840 execution records, 450 T10 ATLIF rows, ten samples with the same ordered 45-context map, 7,318,350 factor tiles and 36,591,750 five-beat output transfers per inference. Independent scheduling reproduces all four serial/candidate cycle pairs and exact speedups. Every context pays one configuration handshake and one release handshake; the candidate additionally pays five fill cycles per context. The final beat is accepted before release, and no compute/output interval crosses a context boundary. Frozen M31 and M37-r10 RTL have compatible T10 result interfaces: 48-bit result and valid-bit fields, 48-bit tags, five beat indices and valid-ready service, with release gated by an empty result FIFO. However, they do not have a matched input/configuration boundary: M31 consumes five 256-bit raw input beats per tile, while M37-r10 is a stage2 sidecar consuming one 384-bit already-produced intermediate; their relevant configuration payloads also differ. M258 fixes both configuration handshakes to one cycle and sweeps no configuration-ready or transfer-bandwidth profile, so it may not call this matched executable-module or configuration-I/O sensitivity. It is only a conditional trace-driven module-cycle sensitivity model. Auxiliary corrections are also required for the producer-stall lower-bound field, actual maximum tag and README beat wording. No system, headline, integrated RTL, throughput/area, energy or PPA claim is admitted.

findings.title: The serial and candidate are not a matched executable input boundary
findings.evidence: The frozen M31 serial engine consumes five 256-bit raw T10 beats and includes stage1 plus stage2. Frozen M37-r10 consumes one 384-bit already-produced INT8 intermediate and is a stage2-only sidecar. Their 48-bit T10 result valid-ready ports are compatible, but M258 does not execute the missing candidate stage1 or a same-input serial/candidate top.
findings.required_fix: Restrict the result to a conditional trace-driven ATLIF cycle model. Build matched raw-input serial and integrated stage1+stage2 candidate tops before claiming an executable module boundary or measured module throughput.

findings.title: Configuration sensitivity is over-admitted
findings.evidence: M258 sets configuration_and_result_backpressure_sensitivity=true, but configuration is a fixed one-cycle handshake in every context and is never swept. The relevant frozen RTL payloads are also not width matched: 750 logical T10 bits for M31 versus 1,104 bits for the M37 stage2 sidecar, before adding the missing integrated candidate stage1 state.
findings.required_fix: Rename this to fixed config/release barrier accounting, or add matched configuration interfaces plus config-valid/ready, bandwidth and latency sensitivity profiles.

findings.title: The producer-stall lower-bound field is not a valid lower bound for two profiles
findings.evidence: M258 subtracts FIFO depth from every context's total service-window nonready cycles, including nonready cycles after production has completed during tail drain. Under the frozen registered FIFO service rule, exact producer stalls are 5,226,609 rather than 5,226,667 at 87.5% ready and 12,196,301 rather than 12,196,504 at 75% ready. The core completion cycles are unaffected.
findings.required_fix: Simulate producer completion and tail drain separately, or relabel the current field as a conservative stall estimate rather than a lower bound.

findings.title: population.maximum_tag is a conservative composite, not the actual maximum tag
findings.evidence: The producer combines context ordinal 44 with the largest tile count from context 0 and reports 739,119,103. Enumerating the disjoint context intervals gives an actual maximum of 738,658,303. No current collision exists because every context has fewer than 2^24 tiles.
findings.required_fix: Compute max((ordinal<<24)+(tiles-1)) over the actual context map and assert tiles<2^24 per context.

findings.title: README misstates the result-beat population
findings.evidence: It calls 36,591,750 entries 'five-beat results'. The trace contains 7,318,350 tile results, each with five beats, for 36,591,750 result beats.
findings.required_fix: Replace the phrase with '36,591,750 ordered result beats' or '7,318,350 five-beat tile results'.

findings.title: The execution is an ATLIF-only compacted projection
findings.evidence: The 45 ATLIF contexts remain ordered and cannot overlap each other, but intervening convolution, attention, FFN and other execution-trace records are omitted. The table is not a wall-clock network schedule.
findings.required_fix: Keep the isolated ATLIF qualifier and do not convert these cycles to network latency or system speedup.

findings.title: Ready sensitivity is limited to four deterministic periodic masks
findings.evidence: The table covers always-ready, single-gap 15/16 and 7/8 masks, and one 12-on/4-off mask. It does not establish arbitrary finite backpressure, randomized traffic, DMA burst distributions or a selected downstream consumer.
findings.required_fix: Retain exact mask names on every number and add selected-consumer or wider adversarial/random ready traces before general I/O robustness claims.

allowed_claims: The frozen H67 ep35 s10 trace has an identical ordered 45-context T10 ATLIF map across ten samples, totaling 7,318,350 factor tiles and 36,591,750 result beats per inference.

For M258's declared conditional schedule with one-cycle configuration and release barriers, the four exact module-cycle ratios are 1.999985x, 1.874988x, 1.749990x and 1.499994x for the named deterministic ready masks.
All 45 contexts drain before release and no modeled ATLIF compute or result service crosses a context boundary.
The frozen serial and stage2-sidecar RTL expose compatible T10 result valid-ready semantics, while their input and configuration boundaries remain unmatched.
A clean producer replay is byte-identical and a wrong execution-trace SHA is rejected before output creation.
forbidden_claims: M258 is matched serial-versus-candidate integrated RTL throughput
M258 models real configuration transfer bandwidth or configuration backpressure sensitivity
The M258 producer-stall lower-bound values are exact for all four profiles
M258 is a full-network wall-clock schedule or system speedup
M258 establishes matched throughput per area, trained rank3 accuracy, power, energy, paper PPA or a headline

next_gate.first: Correct configuration-sensitivity wording, producer-stall accounting, maximum-tag calculation and README beat wording.
next_gate.second: Build one same-raw-input integrated stage1+stage2 candidate boundary against the M31 serial boundary with matched configuration and output ports.
next_gate.third: Replay the 45 contexts with selected downstream ready traces, then run matched Synopsys throughput-per-area before any larger claim.
